title: Taming Recommendation Bias with Causal Intervention on Evolving Personal Popularity

problem.claim: Popularity bias causes popular items to be recommended more frequently than appropriate, harming user experience and recommendation accuracy.

gap.claim: Existing debiasing methods often apply mitigation uniformly across users and only partially account for the temporal evolution of users and items, despite users differing in and changing their preferences for popular items.

contributions.claim: CausalEPP is a method for mitigating recommendation bias by accounting for users' evolving personal popularity.
Evolving Personal Popularity quantifies each user's preference for popular items.
A causal graph incorporates evolving personal popularity into the conformity effect, followed by deconfounded training to mitigate popularity bias.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CausalEPP as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical evaluation finds that CausalEPP reduces popularity bias more effectively than baseline methods and also raises recommendation accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Popularity bias harms user experience and recommendation accuracy.
Existing debiasing approaches insufficiently model user-specific and evolving preferences for popular items.
CausalEPP is proposed to account for evolving personal popularity.
The method measures evolving personal popularity, integrates it into a causal graph, and uses deconfounded training.
Inference uses user-item evolution consistency, and empirical studies report reduced popularity bias and improved accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Users differ in their preference for popular items, and those preferences evolve over time.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation debiasing may benefit from modeling popularity preference as user-specific and time-varying rather than applying uniform corrections.

application.claim: Consider user-specific temporal popularity preferences when designing recommendation-bias mitigation methods.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported empirical studies or recommendation settings.

unknowns: Datasets, experimental settings, and baseline identities are not specified.
Quantitative effect sizes and evaluation metrics are not reported.
The causal assumptions and identification details are not described.
Implementation and reproducibility details are not provided.
